patch.value: Capacity-aware lane admission and continuation packets
Track https://github.com/unbraind/pm-swarm/issues/99 and coordinate with companion item pm-cli-website-8yz0.
Declare and observe windowed capacities, enforce counted admission for next and start, fence interruptions across reclaim, and transfer a bounded continuation packet in Git and shared tracker modes.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Baseline reproduced in a real non-Git tracker: capacity and interrupt were missing, capacity flags on next/start and continuation on brief were rejected, and plain next admitted two workers without a quota bound. Implementing five pushed slices with native revision checks and a real process race.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Slice 1: capacities are native tagged items and each observation is revision-checked and appended to the item history. The read model uses the last two in-window points when both are at most 24 hours old. Revert proof: replacing the forecast with null failed the historical 56 + 8/7 forecast assertion; restored the implementation.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Slice 2: next and start share primary capacity admission with dry-run and report measured refusal context and the next fallback command. Two independent next processes on disjoint work produced one admitted lane and one capacity_exhausted refusal. Revert proof: ignoring occupied slots admitted both workers; the process test failed with exits 0 and 0. The weekly replay produced 57.14 percent and three admitted lanes using the supplied readings and illustrative observation times.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Slice 3: one guarded native mutation records the stopped lane generation and the exhausted window. Reclaim preview and apply preserve the stopped claim until reset. An exact retry appends no duplicate record, and another generation is refused. Revert proof: bypassing the interruption check in reclaim changed the preview from refused to recovered and failed the test.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Slice 4: continuation commits the receiver, new token, capacity binding and packet under one native history guard. The packet replays linked files, sync paths, comments and tests in native order and reports the worktree commit IDs and dirty paths. Revert proof: dropping Git evidence failed the Git packet assertions, and skipping the native transfer failed the history and owner assertions. Independent forecast reverts also proved that disabling staleness or source-label screening fails the capacity test.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Slice 5: the README replay and descriptive help cover capacity admission and transfer. Fair schedule uses the same admission path and retains its flags in fallback commands. Git start also preserves a shared-mode interruption. Revert proof: reverting band help failed the help assertion, and removing the Git start guard caused the interrupted lane restart test to fail.
